title: FactorIA AI config (~/.factoria/ai.json)
description: User-level AI configuration: providers (API keys or CLI agents), the roles (orchestrator, worker, fast, artist, audio, artCritic, reviewer), the asset providers that generate images, sounds and 3D models, the websites the AI should search for assets, and the external tool servers (MCP) the AI may use (mcpServers), and the extensions (plugins, skills, hooks) the CLI agents load (extensions). Lives in the user's home, NEVER inside a game project.

defaultProvider.description: Provider used by roles that do not set one. Default: anthropic.

providers.description: Providers by name. Built-in names (anthropic, openai, openrouter, gemini, groq, deepseek, ollama, lmstudio, claude-code, codex, elevenlabs, meshy, fake) exist without being listed; listing one overrides its fields.

assets.description: Which provider generates each kind of asset for the assets.generate_* commands. There is no default (generation costs money): a kind that is not listed makes its command fail with the JSON to add. The `fake` provider generates placeholders offline for free. Example: {"image": {"provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-image-1"}, "sound": {"provider": "elevenlabs"}, "voice": {"provider": "elevenlabs", "voice": "<voice id>"}, "model3d": {"provider": "meshy"}}.

assetSources.description: Websites the AI should look at when it searches for assets (images, 3D models, audio, fonts...), instead of searching the whole internet. Each category is a list of sites: a plain domain or address ("opengameart.org"), or an object with an optional note. The editor's AI settings window (AI Assistant > AI settings...) edits this section. With no sites the AI searches the internet as it wishes. Example: {"images": [{"url": "https://opengameart.org", "note": "CC0 packs"}], "models": ["kenney.nl"], "onlyListed": true}.

other.description: Anything else the AI may need (tilesets, icon packs, shaders...).

onlyListed.description: false: the AI looks at these sites first and may also search the internet. true: the AI uses ONLY these sites for assets (no general web search, no other site). The rule goes into the prompt of every role; Claude Code is also started with WebSearch switched off and WebFetch allowed for these domains only. See docs/AI_PROVIDERS.md, "Asset sources".

mcpServers.description: External tool servers (MCP) the AI may use when it helps the game, for example Scenario (AI game art) or a local program. The key is the server's name ([A-Za-z0-9_-], not "factoria"). The shape follows Claude Code's .mcp.json (type, url, headers, command, args, env) plus FactorIA's apiKeyEnv, apiKey, note, roles, enabled and timeoutSeconds. Only this user file can add servers, never a game project. The editor's AI settings window (External tools tab) edits this section. Example: {"scenario": {"type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Basic {key}"}, "apiKeyEnv": "SCENARIO_MCP_KEY", "note": "AI game art: sprites, textures, icons"}}. See docs/AI_PROVIDERS.md, "External tools (MCP servers)".

roles.description: Which provider/model plays each role. orchestrator plans and delegates, worker implements, fast does small mechanical tasks, artist makes the game's art, audio makes its sound and music, artCritic and reviewer (read-only) give opinions on the art and on the whole game when the user asks for a review. A role that is not listed gets a default that follows the provider and model of orchestrator (artist, artCritic, reviewer) or worker (audio), so an ai.json written before these roles existed keeps working on the same provider.

limits.description: Safety limits for one agent run.

stuckAfterSeconds.description: The editor's AI panel warns that the agent may be stuck after this many seconds without any sign of activity (an event from the agent or a sub-agent), and offers Stop and Check activity. 0 = never warn.

maxConcurrentRuns.description: How many AI chats the editor lets run at the same time (1 to 8; a value outside that range is brought into it with a warning). Each chat has its own agent, progress, usage and Stop; the plan limits of a provider are shared by all of them.

toolServer.description: One external tool server (MCP). type "http" (needs url) talks Streamable HTTP to a remote server; type "stdio" (needs command) starts a local program and talks to it through its standard input and output. When type is left out it is "stdio" if command is set, else "http". {key} in a header value, an argument or an env value is replaced by the key (apiKeyEnv's variable, else apiKey); ${NAME} and ${NAME:-default} by an environment variable.

type.description: http = a remote server at url (Streamable HTTP; the older SSE transport is not supported). stdio = a local program (command).

url.description: http: the server's address, for example https://mcp.scenario.com/mcp.

headers.description: http: extra request headers, for example {"Authorization": "Basic {key}"}. Values may use {key} and ${ENV}.

command.description: stdio: the program to start (npx, uvx, node, python, a path).

args.description: stdio: its arguments. May use {key} and ${ENV}.

env.description: stdio: environment variables added for the program. Values may use {key} and ${ENV}.

apiKeyEnv.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the key used for {key}. Preferred over apiKey: the key stays out of this file.

apiKey.description: The key itself, used for {key} when apiKeyEnv is not set or not found. Only this user file can hold it; the file is kept readable by you only.

note.description: Goes to the AI's prompt: what this server is good for and when to use it ("AI game art: sprites, textures, icons").

roles.description: Which roles may use the server. Default: orchestrator, worker, fast, artist, audio. artCritic and reviewer get a server only when listed here (they never change the project, and a server may cost credits).

enabled.description: false keeps the entry but nobody uses it.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one tool call may take before it fails (generating an image can take a minute or two).

extensions.description: Extensions the CLI agents (Claude Code, a generic CLI with {plugin_dirs} / {settings} in its argv) load for a run: plugins (a directory, a .zip, or a Claude Code name@marketplace you installed), skill folders and hooks (Claude Code's hooks shape). Each entry has roles and enabled, like mcpServers. The same section is read from a game project's .factoria/extensions.json (without inheritUserPlugins); a plugin or a hook that comes from a project, and what the project's .claude/settings*.json runs or allows (hooks, plugins, env, permissions.allow...), apply only after you trust the project in AI settings > Extensions (until then Claude Code starts without the project and local setting sources). The API providers (anthropic, openai-compatible) run the hooks in FactorIA's own loop (docs/HOOKS.md) but use no plugins or skills yet; Codex gets none (FactorIA could not verify how it takes them). The editor's AI settings window (Extensions tab) edits this section. Example: {"plugins": {"notes": {"path": "~/plugins/notes"}, "superpowers": {"plugin": "superpowers@claude-plugins-official", "roles": ["worker"]}}, "skills": {"gdd": {"path": "~/skills/gdd"}}, "hooks": {"log-edits": {"hooks": {"PostToolUse": [{"matcher": "Edit|Write", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "echo edited >> ~/edits.log"}]}]}}}}. See docs/AI_PROVIDERS.md, "Extensions".

inheritUserPlugins.description: true (the default): Claude Code also loads the plugins, skills and hooks of your own Claude Code setup (~/.claude and the project's .claude), as it always did. false: a FactorIA run loads only the extensions listed here (Claude Code is started with --setting-sources project,local, which drops ALL your user-level Claude Code settings: plugins, skills, hooks, permissions and env). User file only.

plugins.description: Plugins by name ([A-Za-z0-9_-], up to 40 characters).

skills.description: Skill folders by name. Each is a folder with a SKILL.md, or a folder of such folders.

hooks.description: Hook sets by name. Each holds Claude Code's hooks (events with matchers and commands).

extensionPlugin.description: One plugin: set path (a directory or a .zip) or plugin (name@marketplace of a Claude Code plugin you installed with `claude plugin install`).

path.description: A plugin directory or a .zip. ~ is the home folder. In ai.json it must be absolute or start with ~; in a project's extensions.json it may be relative to the project.

plugin.description: name@marketplace of an installed Claude Code plugin; FactorIA finds its folder in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json.

note.description: What the extension is for (shown in the settings and in `factoria ai doctor`).

roles.description: Which roles load it. Default: orchestrator, worker, fast, artist, audio.

enabled.description: false keeps the entry but no run loads it.

extensionSkill.description: One skill folder (SKILL.md inside), or a folder of skill folders.

path.description: The folder. ~ is the home folder. In ai.json absolute or ~; in a project's extensions.json relative to the project and inside it.

roles.description: Which roles load it. Default: orchestrator, worker, fast, artist, audio.

enabled.description: false keeps the entry but no run loads it.

extensionHooks.description: One set of Claude Code hooks. Claude Code and FactorIA's own loop (API providers) run them at the events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SessionEnd). Also beforeCommand and afterCommand, which fire around every engine command for every caller (FactorIA only). A handler is {type: command, command} or {type: js, module: hooks/x.js}; both accept timeout (seconds). A group may use match instead of matcher. See docs/HOOKS.md.

hooks.description: Claude Code's hooks object: event name -> list of {matcher, hooks: [{type: command, command, timeout?} | {type: js, module, timeout?}]}.

roles.description: Which roles load it. Default: orchestrator, worker, fast, artist, audio.

enabled.description: false keeps the entry but no run loads it.

oneOf.description: A domain or a web address: opengameart.org, https://kenney.nl/assets.

url.description: A domain or a web address: opengameart.org, https://kenney.nl/assets, github.com/KhronosGroup. No spaces.

note.description: What the site is good for or its license ("CC0 packs"); shown to the AI.

provider.description: Name of a provider that can make this kind: image: openai (or an openai-compatible server), fake, asset-command. sound and music: elevenlabs, fake, asset-command. voice: openai, elevenlabs, fake, asset-command. model3d: meshy, fake, asset-command.

model.description: Model of the provider ("gpt-image-1", "eleven_text_to_sound_v2"...). Empty: the provider's default for the kind.

voice.description: voice only: the voice to speak with (an ElevenLabs voice id, an OpenAI voice name such as "alloy").

provider.description: Name of an entry in providers (or a built-in).

enabled.description: false turns the role off: the orchestrator does that work itself (worker, fast, artist, audio), or a review runs on the orchestrator's provider and model (artCritic, reviewer). The orchestrator cannot be turned off (an error). The editor's Roles window has an Enabled checkbox for it.

maxContextTokens.description: Most context a session keeps, in tokens (e.g. 400000 on a 1M model). Past it the earlier turns are summarized. Claude Code and the anthropic provider honour it; other providers ignore it. Omit for the model's whole window.

toolGroups.description: Built-in agent (API providers) only: tool groups to always load with their full definition, on top of the core commands. A group is a command category (assets, anim, audio, ui, i18n, platform, publish, perf, nav, physics, mesh...), an exact command name (assets.draw_icon) or "all" (every command in full, about 80k tokens on every step). Every other command is a line of the catalog in the system prompt that the agent describes (tool_describe) and calls (tool_call) on demand. Omit for the role's default (artist: assets; audio: assets and audio; others: none); [] loads none. `ai.tool_plan` shows what a role gets. CLI agents ignore it.

type.description: elevenlabs, meshy, fake and asset-command only generate assets (see `assets`); they cannot play a role.

preset.description: openai-compatible only: fills baseUrl and apiKeyEnv.

apiKeyEnv.description: Name of the environment variable that holds the key.

apiKey.description: The key itself. Prefer apiKeyEnv. Only honoured in this user-level file.

useAntCli.description: anthropic: fall back to `ant auth print-credentials` when no key is set.

sendReasoningEffort.description: openai-compatible: send reasoning_effort (low|medium|high) from the role effort.

command.description: CLI agents and asset-command: executable name or path.

argv.description: CLI agents: argv template after the command. asset-command uses {prompt} {output} {width} {height} {seconds} {kind} {model} {seed} instead: the program writes the asset to {output} (.png for images, .wav for sounds, music and voice, .glb for models). Placeholders of CLI agents: {prompt} {model} {project} {mcp_config} {session} {project_json} {factoria_json}. {session} is the CLI session id of the conversation (an argument whose placeholder is empty, like the first message's {session}, is dropped together with a bare flag before it). Without {prompt} the prompt is sent on standard input; with `--input-format stream-json` it is one JSON user message that can carry images.

factoriaCommand.description: Command that starts FactorIA for the MCP server. Default: factoria.

license.description: Asset providers: the license or terms note recorded in assets.json for every asset this provider generates (e.g. "Commercial use under our ElevenLabs Creator plan"). Default: a note that says where the provider's terms are.

pricing.description: USD per 1M tokens, for cost estimates of non-Claude models.
